items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: So then we got Louis. Then the boat closed.

ctx.x: Well, he must have been a pretty old man by this time. Huh? Charlie McCurdis was pretty old probably by this time.

Well, Charlie McCurdis was. He was much older than you. Oh, yeah. If he's living, he's a pretty old man now. I don't know if he's living. I don't know if he's living, but he's very good. He's one of the earliest. He's a very good climate player. He was. Very, very good, one of your best we had in all of the musicals, you know? So Louis Nelson was the best jazz climate player we had down there. Is that so? Yeah. Charlie McCurdis was the best musician. It's like P. and Pico. Pico was a very good musician, but he's…
Well, when you went on the boat and you started to work, did you go on a trip right away or what?

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: I played almost and played the whole set, man, with that 70-degree band Louie had.

ctx.x: But Mario, we used to sit on and talk.

Now we was together, we'd meet him, never talk about the music. What is when we talk about different things we can understand, what, what, what, what we're playing. Yeah. Pops, since it's not, since it's not we're playing, he says, what you hitting in there? I said, don't hit that, hit this note here. What is it? Hit this note here. Search the ball. Okay, man. Don't look at the wind, what's going on? Remember, just like oil, oil on there. What you mean, Pops? Oh, no. Yeah. I'm like, oh, no. I'm like, oh, no. I'm…
Yeah, all the same style. The same thing, see?

items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: And the biggest thing that I've seen, we were in the Primal Theater, Louie come downstairs with his tails on

ctx.x: Pops, Faust and Muggsy, Spanier, April 21st, 1957, reel three. Did you like the way he played? Oh, yes, I liked the way he played. Did you get together and play a lot together? Oh, yes, we played every night in Chicago. In various clubs? Oh, yes. No, there was a round roll. Oh, there are. Then we'd go out together. We'd go out the south side. And I'd probably go there. We'd sit in there together. I wouldn't care to go. Rap could really play some blues on guitar, couldn't he, Pop? Yeah, that's why I... How good a…

Brown shoes. And the biggest thing that I've seen, we were in the Primal Theater, Louie come downstairs with his tails on, shirt and everything with the pants. And they're blowing his own dress around there. I said, this is where you go on stage. I said, where the hell is your pants? Go to the moon, what the hell you talking about, my brother? That's where you go. How dear to the moon goes to the bamboo

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: Kid O'Reilly. Oh, of course. He's still. Fox Foster.

ctx.x: Kid O'Reilly. Oh, of course. He's still. Fox Foster.

You know what I mean? Well, what about, well, L. Hines is a young one. Yeah. But there ain't a very many that's from that New Orleans guy. No, that's why I'm not. Because most of them are still in New Orleans. They don't want to leave home. And after they come up and stay a while, they get home sick. Well, you know, that's no good.
